record_error_verdicts: I could not see the analyst's own list of record errors: claims.json did not exist in my folder (the folder itself was absent, and I created it) or in the analyst's folder, and facts.md names none as such. The verdicts below cover the record items that facts.md touches, plus those I checked against sources myself.

93.8% sentence (#1 section 7 item 3; wiki conjugate-bounce.md:77, quintessence.md:98, potential-sign.md:66, fate-of-expansion.md:78, lab-notebook.md:91): UPHELD as a record error. [19S] does not assume 'a potential possessing a negative minimum'. It fits a Higgs-like V0 + m^2 phi^2/2 + lambda phi^4/4 with the sign of the minimum left free, and 93.8% is the posterior probability that the vacuum energy is negative: 12.2% de Sitter today with anti-de Sitter later, plus 81.6% 'already being in an AdS phase today' (context_prints.out). The fit is in flat FRW, and the abstract says the transition 'may ultimately lead to' collapse. The figure does not transfer to the program's V0[1+cos] >= 0, whose minimum is zero.

#11 section 10 compound citation '[19S, 20S, 21S]' for 'high posterior preference for a future anti-de Sitter transition and collapse in negative-minimum quintessence fits': UPHELD as a miscitation, if the analyst raised it, and missed otherwise. Only [19S] supports the clause. [20S] (Urena-Lopez et al., DESI-affiliated, arXiv:2503.20178) fits V = m_a^2 f_a^2 [1+cos(phi/f_a)], which has minimum 0, with 'null spatial curvature'. Its TeX has 0 hits for anti-de Sitter, AdS, collapse, crunch and 'negative minimum'; so does the [21S] DESI DR2 TeX (context_prints.out tex counts).

F48, on the diameter note's [S] for Born 1949: PARTLY upheld. The worklog hash exists (notes/phase-space-diameter-worklog.md:86, 9e25ee51...). The retrieval cannot be repeated (the APS PDF returns 403), so the [S] rests only on the record's earlier retrieval. The APS abstract page confirms the title and the date, 1 July 1949.

F64, on the task's 'Comelli, Crisostomi and Pilo 2012': UPHELD. arXiv:1202.1986 is 'Perturbations in Massive Gravity Cosmology', JHEP 06 (2012) 085. The k1 != k2 analysis is in arXiv:1111.1983 (Comelli, Crisostomi, Nesti, Pilo, JHEP 03 (2012) 067). The record (#14 ref [4]; review/v3-worklog.md R7) cites 1202.1986 only for instabilities, which is correct.
F10, DESI DR1 Conclusions sign: UPHELD as an error in the source, not the record. Eq. (24) gives +0.0024 +- 0.0016 and the Conclusions give -0.0024 +- 0.0016.

The diameter note's Born 1938 reading (papers/phase-space-diameter.md section 4: b fixed from the classical electron radius by r0 = h/(pi b), b c = 2 hbar c/r0 ~ 1.4e8 eV): NO ERROR. It is confirmed on the p.298 page image, eqs. (22) and (26), and born1938_b.out gives 'b c = 1.401e+8 eV'.
missed_issues: Bound convention for 'how big is a closed universe': the analyst's curvature_bounds.out takes R_c,min from the closed-side edge of the central 95% interval, and prints 'none' where that interval excludes Omega_K < 0. ACT's own quoted bound (R_k > 105 Gpc) is the 95% quantile among closed samples only; source_conventions.out reproduces 100.7 Gpc that way, against 137.9 Gpc from the central edge. For k = +1 imposed, which is Paul's question, the closed-conditional bound is the relevant one. Gaussian approximation, H0 = 67.4 (closed_conditional_bounds.out): R_c > 100.7 Gpc (P-ACT-LB), 101.0 (DESI DR1+CMB), 124.2 (P-ACT-LB_DR2), 132.4 (DESI DR2+CMB, where the analyst has 'none'), 129.5 (SPT CMB-SPA+DESI, analyst 'none'), 134.0 (Giare+26, analyst 'none'), 77.5 (Planck+lensing+BAO). The analyst's 137.9, 164.0 and 235.7 Gpc overstate the minimum radius.

Gaussian tails misstate Planck's closed preference. curvature_bounds.out lists P(Omega_K<0) = 0.9927 for TT,TE,EE+lowE. The same source says only about 1/10000 samples lie at Omega_K >= 0, and Di Valentino et al. give 99.985%. A Gaussian built from the 68% interval gives P(Omega_K >= 0) = 0.007254 (source_conventions.out), about 50 times the source's tail. Any claim using these Gaussian probabilities for skewed CMB-only posteriors should quote the source's numbers instead.

Missing source: [20S] (Urena-Lopez, Lozano-Rodriguez, Roman-Herrera + 35 DESI builders, arXiv:2503.20178v3, accepted PRD) fits exactly the program's potential, V = m_a^2 f_a^2 [1+cos(phi/f_a)], to DESI DR1 in flat FRW. It finds log10(m_a c^2/eV) = -32.60 +- 0.12 and log10(f_a/M_Pl) = -0.28 +- 0.19 (abstract, retrieved). This is the observational handle on when tau starts oscillating, which sets the turnaround in a closed comatter universe; facts.md does not use it.

Born 1938 stands against the program's slaved momentum metric. Born's p-space metric is 'not directly connected with the metric tensor g_kl in the x-space' (p.292). He wants 'different and widely independent metrics for the two limiting cases' (p.293). His closed momentum space is for 'energetically closed' systems, with b fixed from the electron radius, b c ~ 140 MeV (pp.294, 298). So Born 1938 is no precedent for g~ = g^-1 or for a cosmological b ~ 1/a; all this is verified on the page images.

Born's eq. (9), n = g pi^2 V b^3/h^3, counts one hemisphere of the momentum 3-sphere: the ball |p| < b with measure d^3p/sqrt(1-p^2/b^2) has volume pi^2 b^3, half of 2 pi^2 b^3 (born1938_eq9.out, ratio 0.5). Reading n as the state count of a full S^3 momentum space is off by a factor of 2. The analyst's symbolic check A notes the ratio but facts.md does not.

Low-redshift evidence for an open universe is stronger than facts.md shows. arXiv:2512.19565 (abstract retrieved) reports DESI BAO + SN Ia at 2 sigma for open, over 3 sigma with theta*, and 5 sigma with DESY5. Together with F15, F17 and F18, the current data disfavor a closed universe at roughly 2-3 sigma: Gaussian P(Omega_K<0) is 0.0122-0.0183 for the DR2-era CMB+BAO combinations (closed_conditional_bounds.out).

Planck 2018 equation numbers: ar5iv renders the paper wrongly ('(1), (0a), (0b), (1), ...'). Equations cited by ar5iv number from this paper, the analyst's (44a,b) and (45a,b), are 2 low in the paper's own numbering, (46a,b) and (47a,b). This is reconstructed from LaTeX rules, since the typeset PDF and A&A HTML returned 503/403.

The analyst's downloads include abs_2402.00658.html, an unrelated machine-learning paper ('Learning Planning-based Reasoning by Trajectories Collection...'). Any claim citing arXiv:2402.00658 has a wrong ID; it is probably meant to be 2402.00098, which F60 cites correctly.

F47 says the Born page-image SHA-256 hashes are 'in REPORT.md', but no REPORT.md exists in the analyst's folder, so the image provenance is unrecorded. My scale-2 renderings hash as: leaf_0303 0b54846325fb7b33, 0305 05c6dfb5c9828a0b, 0306 99892cf211b4dd84, 0308 314eec0c5a163de2.

result.overall:
Setup: claims.json was absent. My folder did not exist, so I created it and keyed every verdict to facts.md F1-F67 and N1-N3; the C-numbered claims could not be mapped. Every source was re-retrieved, with each script and its .out saved.

Retrieval: 67 arXiv API records, 35 TeX sources, 7 rendered HTML pages, Crossref, INSPIRE, APS, and the Internet Archive page images of Born 1938.

Quote checks: 83 abstract fragments and 158 body fragments were checked under normalized matching. Every miss was resolved as a rendering difference, a quote from the body rather than the abstract, or a macro, except one wording slip in F45. The bibliographic data all match; the journal references for Majid-Schroers and Mizoguchi-Tada, which the analyst marked dagger, are now verified. The sign convention (closed means Omega_K < 0) is consistent across all sources.

Born 1938: all readings match the page images, as does the record's b c ~ 1.4e8 eV.

Corrections (F1, F3, F15, F45, N1):
- F1, F3: the Planck equation numbers are ar5iv artifacts; the paper's own numbers are (46a,b) and (47a,b).
- F15: the v1 CMB-SPA value was -0.88 +- 0.48, not 0.88.
- F45: the source reads 'behavior ... confidence level'.
- N1: Born did not call b non-universal; he left it open and assumed it universal.

Record: the 93.8% sentence and #11's compound [19S, 20S, 21S] citation are record errors. 93.8% = 12.2% + 81.6% is the posterior for a negative vacuum energy of a Higgs-like quartic in flat FRW. [20S] fits the program's own 1+cos potential, whose minimum is zero, and [21S] says nothing about anti-de Sitter or collapse.

Methodology (in missed issues):
- The analyst's curvature-radius bounds use central 95% edges. For 'if closed, how big' the closed-conditional convention ACT uses applies: R_c > ~100-134 Gpc for current CMB+BAO (Gaussian, H0 = 67.4), not 'none' or 138-236 Gpc.
- Gaussian tails understate Planck's CMB-only closed preference: 0.993 versus the source's 0.9999.
- Current CMB+BAO and low-z data disfavor closure at ~2-3 sigma.
